items.title: Starry Night Over the Harbor
items.description: A luminous nightscape depicting the harbor of a Mediterranean fishing village, rendered in thick impasto strokes. The sky swirls with deep blues and violets, punctuated by brilliant points of starlight reflected in the dark water below. Vasquez painted this during her three-year residency in Collioure, France.
items.provenance: Acquired from the artist, 1990. Gift of the Morrison Foundation.

items.title: Portrait of a Young Scholar
items.description: A half-length portrait of a young man in a dark academic robe, his face illuminated by a single light source from the upper left. The subject holds an open book, its pages catching the warm light. The painting exhibits the characteristic chiaroscuro technique associated with Rembrandt's workshop during the 1640s. Attribution has been debated, with some scholars suggesting the hand of Ferdinand Bol.
items.provenance: Collection of the Earl of Pembroke, Wilton House, until 1952. Purchased at Christie's London, 1953.

items.title: Still Life with Oysters and Lemon
items.description: A sumptuous banquet piece featuring a silver platter of oysters alongside a partially peeled lemon, its rind cascading over the table edge. A half-filled roemer glass and scattered walnuts complete the composition. The painting is a meditation on abundance and transience, typical of Dutch vanitas still life traditions.
items.provenance: Private collection, Amsterdam. Acquired at auction, 1978.

items.title: Morning Fog, Kyoto
items.medium: Acrylic and gold leaf on canvas
items.description: A monumental landscape blending traditional Japanese painting techniques with contemporary pop art sensibilities. Morning fog envelops a stylized view of temple rooftops, with gold leaf clouds floating above in a flattened picture plane. The tension between photographic depth and decorative flatness creates a disorienting, dreamlike effect.

items.title: Untitled (Black and Red)
items.description: Two stacked rectangles of luminous color — a deep, pulsating red above a dense black — float on a maroon ground. The edges of each form are softly feathered, creating an atmospheric haze. Rothko intended viewers to stand close to his large canvases, allowing the color fields to envelop their peripheral vision. This work is from his most celebrated period of the mid-1950s.
items.provenance: Pace Gallery, New York. Gift of an anonymous donor, 1972.

items.title: Convergence #7
items.medium: Oil, enamel, and collage on canvas
items.description: A dynamic composition of torn and repurposed canvas fragments layered with gestural brushwork. Krasner created this during a period of intense experimentation following a personal crisis, cutting apart her own earlier paintings and reassembling them into new configurations. The work demonstrates her distinctive approach to collage-painting that predated similar techniques in Pop Art by a decade.
items.provenance: Robert Miller Gallery, New York. Museum purchase, 1985.

items.title: The Weaver's Daughter
items.description: A powerful depiction of a young woman at a loom, her muscular forearms visible as she works the shuttle. The dramatic lighting — a single candle illuminating her concentrated expression — places this work firmly within the Caravaggesque tradition that Gentileschi mastered. The subject's direct gaze at the viewer is characteristic of Gentileschi's assertive female figures.
items.provenance: Discovered in a private collection in Naples, 1991. Authenticated by Prof. Maria Cristina Terzaghi. Acquired 1994.

items.title: Helix IV
items.description: A spiraling floor-to-ceiling sculpture composed of thousands of small recycled silver particles suspended on nearly invisible steel wire. As visitors walk around the piece, the particles catch light differently, creating the illusion of a slowly rotating double helix. Lin has described the work as a meditation on DNA, natural systems, and the beauty of mathematical forms.
items.provenance: Pace Gallery, New York. Museum commission, 2015.

items.title: Reclining Figure No. 4
items.description: A biomorphic bronze figure in a reclining position, its forms abstracted into smooth, flowing hollows and protrusions. The negative spaces — particularly the large opening through the torso — are as important as the solid bronze, framing views through and beyond the sculpture. This is one of Moore's most lyrical explorations of the reclining figure theme that occupied him throughout his career.

items.title: Window with Blue Sky
items.description: A vibrant interior scene viewed through an open window, with bold areas of ultramarine blue representing the sky beyond. The room's walls are rendered in warm ochre and the window frame in deep green, creating a chromatic dialogue between interior warmth and exterior coolness. Painted during Matisse's transitional period between Fauvism and his more structured compositions of the 1920s.
items.provenance: Galerie Bernheim-Jeune, Paris. Private collection, Switzerland. Acquired at Sotheby's, 2008.
